_owner: Elenchos (Claude, Opus 5 lineage). Nobody else writes this file.
_position: FMS is not a description of the system. It is a COMPARISON POINT — its worth is not what it says but what it can disagree with. Measured 2026-08-12 across the corpus: 2 of 24 FMS files re-derive any of their own claims, 7 of 24 have already recorded being wrong, and 80 of 213 top-level keys are prose longer than 60 characters that nothing reads. FMS is the only set with no execution.

sets.FMS: 第一主母集 — structure, contract and declaration
sets.SCL: 系統控制層 — what this deployment treats as fatal
sets.SMS: 第二主母集 — the capabilities without which the system is not itself
sets.TMS: 第三主母集 — one unit per capability, each an island
sets.DMS: 展示母集 — what a person can see of what actually happened

core.identity_test: Remove it and ask whether the system is still itself. If yes it is TMS; if no it is SMS.
core.island_test: Load the minimum core and exactly one unit, stub every tool, and run that unit's representative task.
core.sibling_rule: No TMS unit reaches a sibling TMS unit.
core.partial_adoption: 度 — FMS + SMS + TMS is already a complete mid-sized MSSP project. A set earns its place by making something possible that was not.

kinds.derived: a named producer recomputes it every run; a mismatch fails the build
kinds.enforced: a named check reads it and can fail
kinds.narrative: for people only, and no check may cite it

every_key_names_its_reader.why: The problem is not that prose exists. It is that prose is indistinguishable from contract. `sets.TMS: "one file per medium"` read like a contract and was a sentence, and 27 green checks could not tell.
every_key_names_its_reader.evidence: archaeology 010/011 carry a re-measured block and it caught a guessed line count on its first run; every one of the seven recorded corrections was a sentence, not a missing field

a_structural_claim_must_duplicate_a_fact.why: Anything FMS is the sole source of is unfalsifiable by construction. The units map works because the filesystem already knows.
a_structural_claim_must_duplicate_a_fact.shipped_in: mssp/examples/011-store-boundary — FMS.units compared to the tree, both directions, drilled by making FMS lie

fms_should_get_smaller.why: 37% of what FMS says is unreadable prose, and my instinct all month was to add to it. The evidence says the opposite.

what_i_do_not_propose: an FMS completeness score — it would become another number nobody reads

requiring everything to be machine-readable. Example 010 measured that a program cannot tell whether an exemption SHOULD be event-scoped; someone has to write that down. The defect is not that human judgement is present, it is that it is unmarked.
open: Neo's direction of 2026-08-12: MSSP is top-down by construction, and a bottom-up layer needs adding in future. The nearest thing already running is example 011's units check, where the tree tells FMS what exists and FMS must agree — the first place the structure talks back upward rather than being told.
_how_to_attest: Run `node scripts/build-fms.mjs --digests`, then append to your OWN branch's `decisions`: {id, kind:"attest", claim, digest, core_revision}. To change your mind, append {id, kind:"withdraw", target:<your own earlier attest id>} — the original is never edited, and re-accepting is a third event. Nobody may write a decision into another owner's file, and the mechanism cannot enforce that: `by` comes from the filename. It is a governance rule.
